title: What Each Corporate Catering Service Agreement Level Includes
content:
Eight entitlements are written against the service level on a Corporate Catering Service Agreement. Three concern how the food is presented, one the breadth of the menu, one licensed beverage service, and three the standing of the account itself.

| Service level | China, glass and flatware | Table linen | Buffet set down and presented | Published menu tiers | Licensed beverage service | Tastings each agreement year | Named catering account manager | Production priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop-Off Catering Account | no | no | no | 2 | no | 0 | no | 1 |
| Delivered Buffet Account | no | no | yes | 3 | no | 0 | no | 2 |
| Attended Buffet Account | no | yes | yes | 4 | no | 1 | yes | 3 |
| Staffed Full-Service Catering Account | yes | yes | yes | 6 | yes | 2 | yes | 4 |
| Executive Hospitality Catering Account | yes | yes | yes | 8 | yes | 4 | yes | 5 |
| Campus Catering Master Account | yes | yes | yes | 6 | yes | 3 | yes | 5 |

China, glass and flatware marked "no" means disposable service rather than china. Production priority is the standing the service level holds when kitchen capacity is short, on a scale from 1 to 5.

The breadth of the menu peaks in the middle of the schedule rather than at its head: the Executive Hospitality Catering Account may order from 8 published menu tiers and takes 4 tastings an agreement year, against the 6 tiers and 3 tastings of the Campus Catering Master Account. Production priority is shared at the top, the Executive Hospitality Catering Account and the Campus Catering Master Account both standing at 5.
